bestBets.overview: THE ROCKET found the line strongly first-up. The rise in trip suits and Chris Parnham goes on. He just needs some luck from a wide draw to go very close. NEWHAVEN PRINCE showed plenty of ability in his initial preparation and attacks this with the benefit of a quiet trial. ALL THE STARS led and ran well on debut. He rolls forward again and can give a big sight. PANCHO'S PLACE next best.

raceTips.comment: THE ROCKET deserves favouritism off his fast finishing second to impressive type Delzee at Northam. Second-up he gets out to a more suitable 1300m, he gains the services of in form senior Chris Parnham and he maps to park in the three deep moving line. Realistically hasn’t had a lot of luck so far his in career with a few handy minors that stand out (third to Rock The Market & Poblano, third to Pure Silver and Naughty Lord). Time to stand up. ALL THE STARS stepped out on debut and led at Pinjarra over 1200m and was only run down late in the race by Unwanted News. Should improve off that performance, should safely get across to at worst park outside the leader and from there should run another honest eachway race. NEWHAVEN PRINCE ran back to back second placings from the breeze in fast run races last prep. WINTER BLOOM ran a cheeky on debut at 200-1.

Newhaven Prince showed plenty of promise in his initial campaign of racing and loved his trial without his race-day shades. The draw and the map is the sticking point but if Noske can find a back or get him across he should give a really good account of himself on return. All The Stars was a great debut. Worked hard to get across and lead, rolled them along at a strong tempo to the corner and kept giving in the run to the line when just overrun late by a nice filly in Unwanted News. Should only take benefit from the run and they’ve stopped the clock 6L quicker than maiden class average. He’s still very raw but he’s clearly got some ability and should be able to work across again here to the breeze. The Rocket worked home well on return into 2nd at Northam over an unsuitable 1100m and can get back in the moving line here blending in out to 1300m, speed on will certainly help his cause as he’ll have some work to do from his likely settling position. Winter Bloom ran a ripper at big odds in debut and only carries 50.5kgs here after Giaan O’Donnell’s claim.

bestBets.overview: TWO UP BOOM should take a stack of beating in this maiden. Last time out he was slow away, settled at the tail, found some traffic problems early in the straight and motored late to finish on the heels of the placings. The rise in trip should be ideal and W Pike goes on. SQUEALER makes her debut on the back of an impressive all the way trial win. Expecting her to park on the speed and give a big kick. SWEET ISSY rolls forward and gives a sight. ABOUT TURN attacks this fresh with the benefit of a solid trial.

raceTips.comment: TWO UP BOOM ran really well first-up in a high rating 3 year old 0MWLY behind Refemme No Angel and dual subsequent winner Flash Dancer and was accordingly plunged in a maiden second-up when the blinkers went on. Stepped slow, laid inwards against Lucy Fiore as she tried to angle outwards for clear galloping room and still was beaten just under a length. Back out in trip, Pike on, drawn to get all the favours, we go again. ABOUT TURN ran second to Natures Reckoning in a 3 year old 0MWLY first-up last campaign and then finished within 1L of Sky Poet second-up. Jefferson Tsang’s claim can allow them to slide forward and put him into the race. STRUT YOUR STUFF had nothing go right for him first-up behind Gentle Touch, Da Hinchi Belle and Rifleman. Late scratching at Pinjarra and now may sneak right under the radar. SWEET ISSY steadily improved at each run last prep and now finds a new home.

Two Up Boom looks to have found his race. Loved the way he attacked the line late first up in 3YO 0MW company in what was a fast run race at 1200m before probably not being suited dropping back to the 1100m last start where he missed the kick badly and did a terrific job to still finish off and get as close as he did in the finish. Out to 1300m here much more suitable, Pike on for the first time this campaign who gets these horses that can be a little tardy out of the gates better than anyone in WA, not an overly strong race. Looks one of the harder horses to beat on the program. About Turn resumes and trialled up really well, ran some solid races last campaign in and around company stronger largely than what he finds here and the 3kg claim of Jefferson Tsang is a nice little luxury to have at the moment, riding very well. Energetic can settle closer here from the draw back to 1300m and has been building nicely this prep, merit to all 3 runs. Squealer trialled up really nicely despite the time being nothing to write home about, looks a debutant with some talent.

bestBets.overview: DESERT ORA produced four straight wins and then last time out she stepped up to Saturday grade and wasn't beaten far after meeting some traffic problems in the straight. Back to midweek grade she should take plenty of beating. POBLANO has been racing well all preparation. W Pike retains the ride. LATE ARRIVAL was sound first-up. He improves off that run and the blinkers go on. PURE MAC has ability and attacks this fresh with the benefit of a solid trial effort.

raceTips.comment: Two horse race according to the market but siding up with the mare on the current second line of betting in Desert Ora. Case to be made she’s in the finish in Saturday 3YO company last start behind Tidwell when not ever really finding clear galloping room in the straight yet was still beaten under 2L and that was off the back of 4 pretty classy wins in a line. Regular rider & the very much in-form Tash Faithfull jumps back on and think if she can find the right trail in the race she’ll be the one presenting late, very progressive mare with more wins in store. Poblano gets the headgear applied for the first time after not being able to get past God’s Gate despite having his back throughout in running last start, was a little disappointed she couldn’t despite the winner franking the form by running well again over the weekend gone. Should have a map advantage on Desert Ora in transit. Late Arrival was a really solid return and has a bit of versatility with the shades also re-applied. Pure Mac resumes having run 3rd beaten 3L in a Lex Piper behind The Crimson Pirate as a 3YO, was always going to need the trial but thought he worked home well.

POBLANO was caught wide early before being sent forward by Pike to find a position. It’s under-rated just how hard that can be for horses to make a ‘secondary’ run in the home straight when asked to extend and you can see in Pike’s body language that he tries to nurse her for as long as possible in the home straight. Was still beaten under 1L and now with blinkers on for the first time she’ll be out to make amends. DESERT ORA won four on the bounce before heading into a 3 year old Saturday when far from disgraced behind Tidwell, Southern Firetail and Western Miss. Swap the barriers, swap the tip. ARMINO actually wasn’t horrible last start. Not too much of a dissimilar run to Yes I Know who bolted in Saturday. LATE ARRIVAL can come out running in an attempt to find the breeze if they wanted too.

bestBets.overview: BUNDABERG attacks this first-up with the benefit of a couple of nice trials. Expecting him to roll forward and give a big kick. STAR SUPREME has been fair in both her starts this time. She should be peaking at her third run back from a spell and the blinkers go on.  DON'T WINK has ability and attacks this first-up with the benefit of two trials. PENNY PINCHER shook her maiden tag last with a solid last start win and has claims again.

raceTips.comment: BUNDABERG has had throat surgery since the Magic Millions. He’s shown X-Factor from time to time, he races on speed and he tried hard to match motors with a handy enough type at Lark Hill trials in Bosisto where they ran time and cleared out from the chasing brigade. DON’T WINK has some wonderful race form to her name: fourth in a Belgravia Stakes behind King Of Light, Snitzalatte and Mardusa, second to subsequent Saturday winning mare Girls Day Out, 3.5L off Twisted Steel and Hubbles Dragon in a Magic Millions. All reads up super, but her trials have only been fair? BRICINI caused a huge boilover to break maiden status in a 5 horse C1 at 70-1. Was it a flash in the pan or was it the run of a mare who is starting to figure it all out? She’ll get a similar run here parked off the back of a spirited tempo. SNIP OF ROMANCE continues to run big races on speed.

Shocking race. Bundaberg is 1 from 11 so he’s hard to tip into with too much confidence but his trial was really good in quick time and he’s a horse that given he can get quite fired up in running should be suited to resuming here over the flying 1000m in a race that looks to have plenty of top end speed engaged. Don’t Wink has comfortably the best race form on the board and I know she’s trialled without her race-day shades on both occasions but they’ve both been very plain efforts and she’s got a 3kg claimer on as a mare who will get off the speed in this field over the 1000m. Great race for her but struggle to trust? Star Supreme gets shades on and the drop back to the 1000m could suit, just not been at her best for a while now? Snip Of Romance knows one way, will pinch one of these soon with her racing pattern.

bestBets.overview: HELLO VENETA was luckless last start at Pinjarra where she didn't get any clear room in the straight. She should be primed for this at her third run back from a spell. PHAT CHAPS is a maiden in a class 1 however he is a horse on the rise and should relish the increase in trip. GLOBAL TRIP rolls forward and gives a big kick.  ROSIE CAN RUN finds it hard to win but will be attacking the line well late.

raceTips.comment: GLOBAL TRIP nearly pinched a 1600m C1 two back behind Forgotten Son and then stepped into an 1800 for the first time in his life. He was free wheeling into the home corner but the gauge read empty over the concluding stages and he was swamped. Back in trip, luxurious 1.5kg claim for Holly Nottle and should stroll his way to the top. In front for a long way from there. ROSIE CAN RUN is 60+ and 3x C3 placed. She put the writing on the wall first-up and should be hard to hold out here. HELLO VENETA ran well fresh at 1200m and then was blocked for clear running the entire length of the straight second-up. Has retuned well and the stable is unstoppable. PHAT CHAPS is looking for ground. If only there was a 1600m maiden on Thursday at Northam….

Another doozey of a race. Phat Chaps is a maiden taking on CL1 gallopers which is never usually a profile I like following in but he’s got some upside and the form out of his initial campaign of racing around horses the likes of King Of Light & Zourun Run still reads up incredibly well when in CL1 company. Raced fresh like a horse looking for further than 1300m despite sticking to 1300m again for his second up run where he was really doing his best through the line, like the rise in trip, the low draw to posi up closer and this really isn’t a strong CL1 at all. Capable of breaking through third up. Hello Veneta trialled really well, ran a super race first up and then never really got a crack at them second up in one of the key form references for this race. If she begins well wouldn’t be surprised to see Brad Parnham come out really positive to park her up right over the speed, the 1650m maybe the only query? Rosie Can Run couldn’t have hit the line better on return, she’s just a mare that has found it very hard to win over the course of her career and lacked that killer blow. Global Trip rolls forward from the draw looking for the front and has been running brave races from there at his past couple. Back to this trip suits.

bestBets.overview: SISTER MARY was very impressive last start at Pinjarra where she settled well off the speed and finished all over the top of her rivals late. If she can repeat that effort she goes close again. WILD THINGS has been solid all preparation and Chris Parnham goes on. SAVIENNE shook her maiden tag two starts back and then was outclassed in the Belmont Classic. LUKA MAGIC next best.

raceTips.comment: SISTER MARY is just a little ripper. Like so many of Paul Jordan’s they have long searching preparations as 2 and 3 year olds and they just seem to get tougher and tougher. After breaking her maiden at 2200m she finished 4L off them in a 54+ and 7.5L off them in a Listed 3 year old event. To most that’s end of prep, but Paul dropped her back in grade, back in distance and she’s back in the winner’s circle. WILD THINGS ran third in an identical version of this race a fortnight ago and she’ll be afforded every chance from a lovely alley. ILGIRO DELMONDO hasn’t fired a shot yet this prep but this is the weakest race she has seen. Expect she’ll find supporters in betting. LUKA MAGIC looks like he’d run another lap. He’ll keep whacking away.

Wild Things was really strong late first time to the 2200m last start at Northam in a race where the winner’s come in 7L faster than the class average, they were really rolling and she closed off as well as anything. These trips look her go and she looks well placed here to be breaking through from another plumb draw in what is a weaker race. Sister Mary is the other still relatively lightly raced galloper in the field who put on a galloping exhibition over the 2200m to break her maiden earlier in the campaign before going on to contest a Belmont Oaks and post another win last start in CL1 company over 1800m chiming in late after getting well back in the field. She looks very dangerous late with a split not doing any work in the run from that low draw. Think the pair with the upside have the edge here over the rest of them. Flash Paddy stuck to his task really well late through that same fast run race that Wild Things comes through last start, getting closer. Dandy’s Gem also through that same race probably just did a bit too much work close to that very strong speed, can be forgiving of one shocker.

bestBets.overview: JUST WALTER JOHN is on the seven day back-up after a solid run here last week. Expecting him to roll forward and give a kick. CHOUX SHOE should improve sharply with W Pike going on for an apprentice. SOLO VEGA charged home and just missed first-up. From a better draw she can settle closer to the speed and run well. PURE OBSESSION found the line strongly at Pinjarra.

raceTips.comment: Another wide open race. Loved the first up run of Solo Vega who really chimed in strongly late for 2nd in some of the best late splits of that entire program despite the tempo of the race being very genuine. Drew 14 of 14 there, draws 3 here to sit closer and while she is up in class into a CL3, there isn’t much difference in depth between the CL1s and CL3s at the moment, lightly raced mare who gives the impression she’s still got some improvement in here. Just Walter John is on trial at the 1400m but he’s been contesting much stronger races than this this preparation and while he did get overrun late last start he did some work to hold the top and went down fighting. Choux Shoe for the kind of mare she is will get on better with William Pike than anyone else, dangerous with a late split from 3-4 back the fence, especially if there is genuine tempo. Pure Obsession came on massively second up the way he finished off and is dropping back to CL3 company here so he’s well placed, just worried about how far back he’s going to get once again here from the draw?

SOLO VEGA was huge at her return to racing. She missed the kick, found herself last and came charging down the centre of the track at Pinjarra to miss by a head. Boy Hill threw her into a Breeders Classic, a Challenge Stakes and a Natasha Stakes when last in work, so clearly there’s an opinion of her and if she can reproduce that run, she’ll go very close here at an eachway price. JUST WALTER JOHN is on the 7-day spin, they again swap blinkers for visors and he’ll likely lead uncontested. Just can’t quite find the right set up for him at the moment, but he’s going well. CHOUX SHOE hasn’t had much go her way since the dynamic fresh win.  PURE OBSESSION bounced back to a level of form last start and sneaks back in grade.

bestBets.overview: DELZEE is a promising type who shook his maiden with a strong last start win. From his inside draw he can stalk the speed and go very close. HEZ GOT THE SAFE will appreciate the drop in class. He does find it hard to win but will be attacking the line strongly. CATCH CARTER rolls forward and gives a kick. BELAURA STAR should improve on his first-up run and has claims.

raceTips.comment: Tough race after tough race after tough race this Wednesday. Acta Non Verba makes his WA debut off a really nice trial leading in as a horse who placed in BM78 company over in Victoria and contested G2 & G3 races early in his career. His best form over there is pretty good, easily good enough to be stacking up in a field like this and while he might not be fully wound up having his first run back, he could have a class edge on these. Catch Carter drops back to CL3 company after setting a red-hot tempo in CL5 company last start over 1300m and only getting overrun very late by God’s Gate who franked that form in Saturday company last weekend. Reckon the drop back to 1200m will suit him too and he doesn’t need to lead either to be in the finish. Hez Got The Safe has been a hard horse to catch over the course of his career, the ability is there but the penny may never drop and the draw makes his task even tougher here. Divine Impact an improver second up, back in grade out to 1200m. Winning chances certainly don’t end there in a dartboard job to finish.

DELZEE is a nice horse in the making. He led and won his 930m Lark Hill barrier trial but looked very green and raw. On debut he couldn’t reel in speedy subsequent Saturday winner Dawn Dancer and then second-up he was still green and wayward in the straight but he bolted in by 1.5L. Should the runner-up (The Rocket) win the opener the form will only look stronger and hopefully a rail to follow will only see him continue to improve. ACT NON VERBA is a big watch at his WA debut. He is BM78 (~66+) placed and has raced in a Group 2 and a Group 3 in Victoria. Respect. CATCH CARTER fought on for a long time behind Gods Gate and Poblano in a C5 last time out. HEZ GOT THE SAFE drops back into a C3. 7 of his last 9 have been in higher grade and he had genuine excuses first-up in the In Confidence race.
